_: The crowd thinks out loud (RCT's guest thoughts, Theme Hospital's patients; PLAN.md, fun audit item 5). A ruling, and a town's hunger, siege or levy, start a rumour in that town; travellers carry it on (chatter.js). With Off Grid AI running, Omni words it; without, these lines. Tune here, not in code. rumourSeasons: seasons a rumour keeps travelling after someone heard it (chatter.js).

helped: The King stood by {house}, they say.
{house} did well at court, and they carry it high.
The crown has been kind to {house}. Kinder than to us.
{house}'s steward walked the market today like a lord himself.
Whatever {house} asked, they say the King gave it.
Fortune favours {house} this year. May some of it fall our way.
{house} rode home from Kingsmere with their banners high.
hurt: The King is no friend to {house} now.
{house} came away from court with nothing.
They say {house} are sore at the crown.
Mark me, {house} will not forget this.
{house}'s men drink hard tonight, and say little.
The King turned {house} away. That will cost someone.
Nobody in {house}'s hall speaks the King's name kindly now.
{house} were shamed at court. Shame keeps a long count.
plain: The King has ruled on it. We will see what comes.
Court has spoken. Nobody asked us.
Another ruling from the castle. Bread costs the same.
Lords quarrel, the King judges, and the plough still wants pulling.
Whatever the King decided, the rent is due at harvest-tide all the same.
The crier read the King's judgement in the square. Few stopped to hear it.
Judgements at court. Here the well still wants a new rope.
They say the King sat late at court. The harvest does not wait on him.

hunger: Bread is dear and the granary is bare.
The King fed someone. Not us.
We ate the last of the seed corn. What do we sow in spring?
The miller's wheel stands still. Nothing comes to grind.
Thin soup and thinner bread, and winter not yet half done.
They are boiling nettles in the lanes now.
The baker puts sawdust in the loaves, and charges more for them.
siege: Nobody gets in or out. How long can we hold?
The walls are full of soldiers and the larder is empty.
They say the King's host is coming. Pray it comes in time.
Their fires ring the town every night. Closer each time.
The well water tastes of the dead.
We pulled down the stables to feed the fires.
A stone from their engine took the bell tower this morning.
The captain says hold. The captain eats better than we do.
levy: They took my boy for the King's host.
Half the men gone to the levy. Who brings the harvest in?
Banners and drums. The levy is marching.
The sergeant counted every man who can hold a spear.
My husband took his father's old sword. It was rusted through.
The levy left at dawn. The women did the ploughing by noon.
Two seasons, they said. They said that last time.
The road is all carts and spears, and no one coming home.

omni.system: You are a townsperson in a medieval town called {town}. Say one short sentence of street talk about what the King just did, blunt and plain, in your own voice. No quotation marks.
omni.prompt: The King ruled: {ruling}. {who} How does the town take it? One sentence.
